key_equations_and_data: SENSOR SCHEMA (§12.2, lines 826-898): top-level key `sensor` with blocks `name`, `band`, `optics`, `fpa`, `noise`, `nuc`, `isp`, `outputs`. band.lambda_min_um, band.lambda_max_um (§12.1 table line 805: NIR 0.75-1.0, SWIR 0.9-1.7, MWIR 3.0-5.0, LWIR 7.5-13.5 um; §5.2 line 285-290 gives slightly different nominal ranges). Constraint lambda_max > lambda_min, both within WAVELENGTH_MIN_UM..WAVELENGTH_MAX_UM.

band.spectral_response: path to CSV of (lambda_um, R) — R(lambda) is the normalised spectral response = QE x filter x window (§2 symbol table line 101). Convention decided in ir-radiometry skill lines 133-135: normalised to PEAK 1.0, absolute responsivity lives in the detector model; loader must assert peak == 1.0, lambda strictly increasing, 0.1 <= lambda <= 100 um (skill line 37-38), 0 <= R <= 1.

fpa.frame_rate_hz -> Delta_t = 1/frame_rate (§9.2 line 637 bolometer IIR S_n = S_{n-1} + (S_ideal - S_{n-1})(1 - exp(-Delta_t/tau_th)); 60 Hz with tau_th = 10 ms smears ~0.6 frames, line 634).

outputs.radiance_linear (float32 W m^-2 sr^-1), outputs.apparent_temperature (float32 K), outputs.dn_16 (uint16), outputs.display_8 (RGBA8) (§12.2 lines 893-897; §13.4 line 1027 IrRadiance / IrApparentT / IrDN16 / IrDisplay8). Non-negotiable #2: the two float outputs are float32 minimum — the schema must not allow a dtype knob below float32.

MATERIAL SCHEMA (§12.3 lines 906-920): `materials.<name>.thermal {density_kg_m3 rho, specific_heat_j_kgk c_p, conductivity_w_mk k, thickness_m delta, solar_absorptivity alpha_sol}` feeding C = rho c_p delta [J m^-2 K^-1] (§6.1 line 351), thermal inertia P = sqrt(k rho c_p) (§6.3 line 394), R_12 = delta_1/(2k) + delta_2/(2k) (§6.4 line 412); §6.2 table lines 372-379 is the minimal parameter set (h is derived, not authored). `optical {spectral_emissivity: csv path (lambda_um, eps(lambda)) over 0.3-15 um; roughness_per_band {nir, swir, mwir, lwir} decreasing with wavelength (§4.3 line 256, §12.3 line 922); angular_model {type: fresnel, n_k_file} | empirical {eps0, a in 0.15-0.35, p in 4-6} | constant (§4.2 Levels A/B/C lines 217-248); transmittance_per_band {nir, swir, mwir, lwir} (§4.4 line 260)}`. thermal-materials skill lines 137-150 adds `source: measured|literature|estimated`.

Kirchhoff closure eps + rho + tau = 1 per band to 1e-6 absolute (§4.1 lines 203-211 'author one, derive the other'; §4.4; §15 Tier 1 line 1182; CLAUDE.md #4). Schema rule: exactly one of spectral_emissivity / spectral_reflectance may be authored; rho is derived as 1 - eps - tau; validator rejects eps(lambda) + tau_band > 1 + 1e-6 anywhere in the band.

Band identity: canonical BandId set {nir, swir, mwir, lwir} used as keys of every per-band material dict (§12.3 lines 917-919). Default regime per band from §12.1 line 810-811 (NIR/SWIR reflective, MWIR mixed, LWIR emissive); default detector model from §12.1 line 808 (photon, photon, photon, bolometer). The §12.2 sensor schema has NO explicit band id field — the link from a sensor's lambda range to the material dict key is undefined.

§16.2 lines 1262-1278 starting material values (eps_LWIR, eps_MWIR, alpha_sol, rho, c_p, k) for 15 materials — scalar per band, literature estimates; the §12.3 schema expects a spectral CSV, so the schema must decide whether scalar-per-band emissivity is an accepted fallback (Appendix A #3 line 1388 says emissivity is grey within a band anyway).

LUT DATA CONTRACT (§3.2(b) line 164; generate_luts.py docstring; ir-radiometry skill lines 63-66): T grid [200, 1000] K at 0.05 K -> 16001 entries per table; float32; three tables Lb [W m^-2 sr^-1], Lb_q [ph s^-1 m^-2 sr^-1], dLb_dT [W m^-2 sr^-1 K^-1] (§3.4 line 188 tabulate alongside); Simpson quadrature of R(lambda) x Planck on a 0.01 um grid; files `data/lut/<sensor>_{Lb,Lb_q,dLb_dT}.npy` + sidecar `<sensor>_lut.json` carrying SHA-256 of the config and the spectral file so a stale LUT is detected rather than silently wrong. Tolerances: LUT vs quadrature < 5 mK equivalent; inverse round trip < 1 mK; Lb strictly increasing (§15 Tier 1 lines 1179-1181).

Cross-check identity for the spectral-response loader and the LUT script: for a rectangular R(lambda) on [lambda1, lambda2], integral R B dlambda must equal band_radiance_tophat(lambda1, lambda2, T) = (sigma T^4/pi)[F(lambda2 T) - F(lambda1 T)] to 0.1% (§3.2(a) lines 150-162; generate_luts.py lines 15-16).

Temperature encoding constants coupled to the LUT range: c = (T - T_ref)/T_span with T_ref = 200 K, T_span = 800 K (§13.3 line 981; isaac-sim-spg skill line 104) — the LUT domain [200, 1000] K is exactly T_ref .. T_ref + T_span; must be defined once (constants) and shared by config, radiometry and irsim_isaac.

ATMOSPHERE PRESET DATA (schema not given by spec; directory `configs/atmospheres/` exists; CLAUDE.md layout assigns atmosphere YAML schema to config/): per-band gamma_B [m^-1] indexed by (band, atmosphere, humidity, visibility) (§7.2 lines 469-471); LWIR humidity form gamma_LWIR ~ gamma_0 + beta w with w = 216.7 RH e_s / T_K g m^-3, e_s(T) = 6.112 exp(17.67 T_C/(T_C + 243.5)) hPa (§7.3 lines 494-501); tau(d) = exp(-gamma d) (§7.1 line 451). Known-answer table §7.2 lines 475-481: clear-dry LWIR tau@200 m 0.90-0.96, humid 0.72-0.85, light fog (200 m vis) LWIR 0.35-0.60 / MWIR 0.25-0.50 / SWIR 0.10-0.30, dense fog LWIR 0.02-0.10. Sky model parameters that may live in the preset: T_sky(theta_el) = T_air - DeltaT_clear (1 - cloud) cos^q(theta_el), DeltaT_clear 55-70 K, q 0.5-1.0 (§5.3 lines 310-314). Non-negotiable #6: T_air, RH, cloud must come from the injected WeatherSeries, never from the preset.

WEATHER SERIES FIELDS (thermal-solver skill lines 97-98; §6.4 line 414 spin-up 24-48 h; Appendix A #8 'weather is prescribed'): time (hourly, monotonic), air temperature [K], relative humidity [0-1], wind speed [m/s >= 0], cloud fraction [0-1], direct and diffuse solar irradiance [W m^-2 >= 0, direct normal <= ~1361 W m^-2 — solar constant not yet in constants.py and must be added there with a source], optional precipitation. Location `data/weather/`.

NIGHT/SOLAR ILLUMINATION PARAMETERS referenced by §12.2 line 900 ('enable the night-illumination model') but absent from the schema: E_airglow level default ~10 nW cm^-2, range 3.5-39 (§5.5 line 338), k_cloud, moon phase, E_artificial (§5.5 line 335); solar term E_sun, shadow S (§5.4 line 323).

Reference camera known answers for config tests (§16.1 lines 1245-1256): VOx, 640x512, 12 um pitch, NETD <60/<50/<40 mK, band ~7.5-13.5 um, 60 Hz, 14 mm lens 32 deg HFOV, tau_th 8-12 ms, TCR ~ -2%/K. §6.4 line 412: C_1 ~ 5 kJ m^-2 K^-1 for thin painted metal (car_paint_black in §12.3 gives 7800*470*0.0012 = 4399 J m^-2 K^-1).

work_items.description: Create `src/irsim/config/sensor.py`: `SensorConfig` with nested `BandSpec`, `OpticsSpec`, `DistortionSpec`, `FpaSpec` (discriminated union on `type`: `BolometerFpa` requires thermal_time_constant_ms/tcr_per_k and forbids photon fields; `PhotonFpa` requires quantum_efficiency/well_capacity_e/integration_time_ms/dark_current_model), `NoiseSpec` + `Ratios3D` (tvh must be exactly 1.0, all >= 0), `NucSpec`, `IspSpec`, `OutputsSpec`. Cross-field validators: lambda_max > lambda_min within constants bounds; regime consistent with wavelength (emissive forbids lambda_max < 2.5 um; reflective forbids lambda_min > 3 um); clip_percentiles ordered in [0,1]; cold_shield_efficiency in [0,1]; transmittance in (0,1]; fill_factor in (0,1]; bit_depth 8..16; bad_pixel_fraction in [0,0.01]. Read-only derived properties: `pixel_area_m2`, `nyquist_cyc_per_mm`, `hfov_deg`, `frame_period_s`, `dn_max`. Deliberately NO aperture-factor property (non-negotiable #5). Add a `schema_version: int` field. Also in this commit: make `make typecheck` pass by adding `types-PyYAML` to dev deps (or a `yaml.*` mypy override — record which in the commit body), add a `config` row to the README status table, CHANGELOG entry. Do not yet load YAML (BC-02) — build models from dicts here.

decisions_needing_adr.title: Config schema technology and strictness (pydantic v2, extra='forbid', frozen models, units-in-field-names, schema_version)
decisions_needing_adr.why: Every downstream module reads these objects and every golden fixture/LUT sidecar embeds their hash; changing the validation model later invalidates fixtures and silently changes which YAML files are accepted. Strict rejection of unknown keys is what prevents a typo like `f_stop` from defaulting F and producing a 20-100% radiometric error.
options: pydantic v2 BaseModel with extra='forbid', frozen=True, Literal enums, field validators (already a dependency; mypy strict may need the pydantic.mypy plugin)
stdlib dataclasses + hand-written validation (no new dependency semantics, more code, weaker error messages)
attrs + cattrs (not in pyproject; adds a dependency)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Data path resolution root for spectral_response, n_k_file, spectral_emissivity and weather files
decisions_needing_adr.why: The spec (§12.2 line 832 `responses/…`), the YAML (`spectra/…`), generate_luts.py (`data/spectra/`) and the ir-radiometry skill (`data/spectra/<detector>.csv`) disagree today and the referenced file does not exist. Whatever is chosen is baked into every config file and every hash.
options: Relative to a single data root (`<repo>/data`, overridable by argument and IRSIM_DATA_DIR) — recommended; matches generate_luts.py and the skill
Relative to the YAML file's own directory (portable bundles, but configs/ and data/ are separate trees today)
Absolute paths only (breaks across machines and CI)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Canonical config hash definition (what is hashed, how floats/paths are canonicalised, band_hash vs config_hash)
decisions_needing_adr.why: The hash is written into LUT sidecars (§3.2(b)/skill) and golden fixtures (ir-sim-testing skill) and must stay stable for the life of the repo; a hash that covers too little reuses stale LUTs silently, one that covers too much (e.g. NETD grade) forces needless regeneration and breaks LUT sharing across the §16.1 60/50/40 mK variants.
options: SHA-256 over canonical JSON of the validated model with file paths replaced by content SHA-256; separate band_hash over band block + spectral file only (recommended)
SHA-256 of the raw YAML bytes (fragile: comments/key order change the hash)
Hash only the spectral file (misses lambda range and regime changes)

decisions_needing_adr.title: LUTs committed to git vs generated on install/CI
decisions_needing_adr.why: .gitignore excludes data/lut/*.npy|*.json while the ir-radiometry skill says LUTs are 'checked into data/lut/ with a hash'. The choice determines whether a fresh clone can run the radiance kernel without running `make luts`, and whether LUT regeneration diffs are reviewable.
options: Commit the 3 x 64 kB float32 tables + sidecar per band and keep the stale-hash check as the guard (skill's position)
Keep them gitignored; `make install` and CI run `make luts`; tests generate into tmp_path (current .gitignore position)
Commit only the sidecar JSON, regenerate arrays on demand

decisions_needing_adr.title: Band identity: explicit `band.id` in the sensor YAML vs derived from the wavelength range; canonical nominal ranges
decisions_needing_adr.why: Per-band material dicts (§12.3) are keyed by {nir,swir,mwir,lwir} but §12.2 gives the sensor no band id; §12.1 and §5.2 also disagree on nominal ranges (SWIR 0.9-1.7 vs 1.0-1.7 (ext 2.5); LWIR 7.5-13.5 vs 8-12). The mapping decides which material roughness/transmittance a camera sees and outlives every config.
options: Optional explicit `band.id` validated against derivation by maximal overlap with §12.1 ranges (recommended)
Always derived, never authored (fails for unusual filters, e.g. 1.8-2.6 um extended SWIR)
Always explicit, no derivation (simple, but allows a mismatched id to go unnoticed)

decisions_needing_adr.title: R(lambda) normalisation and where quantum efficiency lives
decisions_needing_adr.why: §9.1 line 603 permits folding eta into R(lambda); §2 line 101 defines R as QE x filter x window; the ir-radiometry skill mandates peak-normalised R with absolute responsivity in the detector model. Choosing wrong double-counts or drops QE in every photon-band NETD prediction, and the choice is embedded in every spectral CSV.
options: R(lambda) peak-normalised shape (may include QE spectral shape) + scalar `fpa.quantum_efficiency` as absolute peak QE (recommended; matches skill and the existing generate_luts docstring)
Absolute R(lambda) (peak = QE) with no separate eta field (breaks the peak==1 assertion and the bolometer/photon symmetry)
Shape-only R with QE entirely spectral in a second file (more faithful, more data nobody has)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Shared home for T_REF/T_SPAN encoding constants and the LUT temperature grid
decisions_needing_adr.why: §13.3 defines T_ref = 200 K, T_span = 800 K; §3.2(b) defines the LUT domain [200, 1000] K; they are the same numbers defined in two sections and will be used by config (sidecar), radiometry (grid) and irsim_isaac (encode/decode kernels). Defining them twice is how the encode/decode round trip drifts.
options: Add T_ENCODE_REF_K, T_ENCODE_SPAN_K, LUT_T_MIN_K, LUT_T_MAX_K, LUT_DT_K to irsim.radiometry.constants with §3.2/§13.3 citations (recommended)
Make them fields of the sensor YAML (allows per-sensor ranges but lets two sensors disagree with one encoder)
Hard-code in each consumer (status quo in the spec; rejected by CLAUDE.md 'don't invent constants')

decisions_needing_adr.title: Material schema split and fallbacks: config/ owns schema, materials/ owns loader+library; `source` field; scalar per-band emissivity fallback; `materials:` wrapper key
decisions_needing_adr.why: CLAUDE.md layout puts 'pydantic schemas for material YAML' in config/ and 'library + loader' in materials/; the spec §12.3 shows a `materials:` wrapper and a spectral CSV while §16.2 provides only scalar per-band values and Appendix A #3 concedes emissivity is grey within a band. The team needs one answer before the first material file is authored, because retrofitting (§4.4 line 260) is painful.
options: Schema in config/ with optional scalar `emissivity_per_band` fallback (validated against closure) and mandatory `source`; loader/library/closure walk in materials/ (recommended)
Spectral CSV mandatory from day one (blocks authoring until spectra exist for 15 materials)
Everything in materials/ (contradicts CLAUDE.md layout)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Atmosphere preset parameterisation
decisions_needing_adr.why: The spec gives no YAML for configs/atmospheres; §7.2 says 'store a small table indexed by (band, atmosphere, humidity, visibility)' while §7.3 gives gamma = gamma_0 + beta w. The preset schema fixes which of these the atmosphere module receives, and non-negotiable #6 requires that humidity/T_air never be preset fields.
options: Per-band (gamma_0, beta) with w computed from the injected WeatherSeries via Magnus (recommended; smallest schema, satisfies #6 by construction)
Per-band tau at a reference range plus visibility scaling (matches published curves directly, humidity handled ad hoc)
Full (band, humidity, visibility) lookup table (MODTRAN-derived; more data than exists today)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Policy for §12.2 schema gaps: housing temperature parameters, radiometric flag, night/solar illumination block, shutterless residual parameters, distortion coefficient conventions
decisions_needing_adr.why: `housing_temp_mode: fixed` has no temperature; `coupled` has no thermal parameters (§8.2/§9.2); §11.1 and the sensor-noise-chain skill require a 'radiometric' declaration the schema lacks; §12.2 line 900 says to 'enable the night-illumination model' but no field exists; Brown-Conrady/Kannala-Brandt coefficient counts differ. Extending the schema now vs deferring changes every config file and hash.
options: Extend now with optional, defaulted fields (`optics.housing_temp_k`, `optics.housing_tau_s`, `radiometric: bool`, `illumination: {airglow_nw_cm2, moon, artificial}` or move illumination to a scene config) and a schema_version bump (recommended)
Defer until the consuming module lands, accepting a hash-breaking schema change later
Put scene-level items (illumination, sky) in a separate scene/environment YAML from the start

decisions_needing_adr.title: Dev dependency for PyYAML typing (`types-PyYAML` vs mypy ignore_missing_imports override)
decisions_needing_adr.why: mypy strict on src/irsim will fail on the first `import yaml`; the choice adds a dependency to pyproject and outlives the commit.
options: Add `types-PyYAML` to the dev extra (typed, recommended)
Add `yaml.*` to the mypy ignore_missing_imports override (untyped calls into yaml)

decisions_needing_adr.title: LUT file naming and sharing: per-sensor vs per-band-hash
decisions_needing_adr.why: generate_luts.py names files by sensor; two sensors sharing a detector (Boson consumer/professional/industrial NETD grades, §16.1) would duplicate identical tables and the isaac loader must know which file a sensor uses.
options: Name by band_hash prefix with a sensor->hash map in the sidecar (dedupes; recommended)
Name by sensor (simple; duplicates)
Name by BandId only (breaks when two LWIR cameras have different R(lambda))

ambiguities_and_risks.description: LUT generation uses the 'sensor' as the LUT key, but the LUT depends only on the band block + spectral file; the isaac kernel (§13.5) loads one table per band — the sensor->LUT mapping and sharing across NETD variants are undefined.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: BC-08 test_two_sensors_same_band_share_band_hash; confirm the isaac loader looks up by band_hash from the sidecar rather than by sensor name.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: `bit_depth` vs `outputs.dn_16`: for a 14-bit ADC (§11.3 '14-16 bit'), whether DN16 is left-shifted, zero-padded or clipped is undefined; the schema must allow bit_depth 8..16 while the isp area defines DN16 container semantics.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Add a 14-bit variant config in tests; the isp area's Tier 2 SITF test must show DN16 = DN14 << 2 (or documented alternative) and no wrap-around (sensor-noise-chain skill 'Well saturation').

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Per-band material dicts require all four BandId keys per the §12.3 example, but early on only LWIR is configured; whether a material missing `swir` fails at load or only at use is a policy choice that affects authoring friction.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: BC-05 enforces all four keys at load (spec example shape); revisit if the material audit script (thermal-materials skill) shows authoring friction, and record the change in the material-schema ADR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Night-illumination/solar parameters (§5.4, §5.5: airglow level 3.5-39 nW cm^-2, cloud factor, moon phase, artificial sources) are named as something to 'enable' for SWIR (§12.2 line 900) but have no home in any schema; they are scene/environment properties, not camera properties.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Decide in the schema-gaps ADR whether they live in a scene/environment YAML alongside the atmosphere preset; verify with the Tier 3 item 'SWIR at night is usable from airglow alone' once the scene radiance area lands.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: HFOV derived from the YAML (640 x 12 um, f = 14 mm -> 30.7 deg) differs from §16.1's datasheet 32 deg by 4%; either the lens EFL differs from 14 mm or the datasheet HFOV is a rounded/diagonal figure.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Check the FLIR Boson 640 14 mm lens datasheet (EFL vs nominal focal length); keep the BC-01 test tolerance at 5% and tighten once the true EFL is known.

non_negotiables_touched: #1 Engine-free core: `src/irsim/config/` uses only pydantic, PyYAML, NumPy and stdlib; `tests/unit/test_layering.py` already rglobs every `src/irsim/**/*.py` so each new config module is checked automatically for omni/pxr/isaacsim/warp/carb imports. Additionally config must never import `irsim_isaac` — add that root to the FORBIDDEN set in the same step (BC-01).

#2 float32 or better: the LUT sidecar records `dtype: float32` and `load_lut_bundle` asserts `np.float32` and shape (16001,) (BC-08 tests test_generated_boson_lut_is_float32_16001 and test_lut_loader_rejects_float16_bundle); `OutputsSpec` exposes no dtype knob below float32 for radiance_linear/apparent_temperature; the spectral response loader returns float64 for quadrature (BC-03).

#3 Noise in radiance/electron space: not enforced by config code, but `noise.netd_mk_at_300k` is documented in the schema as a Kelvin-space CALIBRATION ANCHOR consumed only through dLb_dT at 300 K (§9.4), never as a Kelvin sigma; the field name keeps the 300 K reference explicit. Enforcement lives in the noise area's 'NETD decreases with scene temperature' test.

#4 Kirchhoff closure: `MaterialConfig` forbids authoring emissivity and reflectance together and rejects eps(lambda) + tau_band > 1 + 1e-6 (BC-05 tests test_authoring_emissivity_and_reflectance_together_is_rejected, test_closure_impossible_rejected); the full-library walk test that CLAUDE.md requires is owned by the materials area and depends on this schema.

#5 Aperture factor pi/(4F^2+1) defined once in irsim.optics: config stores `f_number` only and provides no aperture/omega property; BC-01 test_config_exposes_no_aperture_factor greps the config package for any such computation.

#6 One WeatherSeries feeds thermal and atmosphere: `AtmospherePreset` is `extra='forbid'` with an explicit rejection of air-temperature/humidity/wind/cloud keys (BC-06 test_preset_rejects_weather_fields), so weather can only enter through the injected object; the weather file loader (BC-07) returns plain arrays and constructs neither solver nor atmosphere. The constructor-level enforcement test belongs to the thermal area.
spec_internal_inconsistencies: Spectral response path: docs/physics-model.md §12.2 line 832 `spectral_response: "responses/boson_vox.csv"` vs configs/sensors/flir_boson_640_lwir.yaml line 13 `spectra/boson_vox.csv` vs scripts/generate_luts.py line 7 `data/spectra/` vs .claude/skills/ir-radiometry/SKILL.md line 121 `data/spectra/<detector>.csv`. The file exists under none of these paths (data/spectra/ holds only .gitkeep).

LUT storage: .gitignore lines `data/lut/*.npy` and `data/lut/*.json` exclude generated LUTs, while .claude/skills/ir-radiometry/SKILL.md lines 65-66 say the LUT is 'checked into data/lut/ with a hash of the config that produced it'.

Photon fields: §12.2 lines 858-861 list `quantum_efficiency`, `well_capacity_e`, `integration_time_ms`, `dark_current_model` as `null` for a bolometer; the YAML omits them entirely (lines 27-36). The schema must accept both forms (Optional, default None).
Distortion example: §12.2 line 843 `coeffs: [-0.28, 0.09, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]` vs YAML line 24 all zeros marked ESTIMATED — the spec's numbers are illustrative, not Boson data; neither cites a source.

Band nominal ranges: §12.1 line 805 SWIR 0.9-1.7 um, LWIR 7.5-13.5 um vs §5.2 lines 288-290 SWIR 1.0-1.7 (ext. 2.5) um, LWIR 8.0-12.0 (7.5-13.5) um. A band registry must pick one (recommend §12.1, the configuration section).

Night illumination: §12.2 line 900 says adding SWIR means 'enable the night-illumination model', and §5.5 line 338 calls the airglow level 'configurable', but the §12.2 schema (lines 826-898) has no illumination/airglow/solar field anywhere.

Radiometric flag: §11.1 line 755 and .claude/skills/sensor-noise-chain/SKILL.md line 157 ('A camera config declares whether it is radiometric') require a config declaration that §12.2 does not contain; `outputs.apparent_temperature` is the only proxy.

Housing temperature: §12.2 line 839 offers `housing_temp_mode: fixed | ambient | coupled` but no housing temperature value for `fixed` and none of the T_FPA lumped-model parameters §9.2 line 644 calls for under `coupled`.
Palette list: §11.4 line 792 names 'Ironbow, Rainbow, Lava, Arctic'; §12.2 line 891 offers `gray | ironbow | rainbow | lava` (adds gray, drops arctic).

QE placement: §9.1 line 603 'eta the quantum efficiency (folded into R(lambda) if you prefer)' vs §2 line 101 'normalised spectral response (QE x filter x window)' vs ir-radiometry skill lines 133-135 'R(lambda) is normalised to peak 1.0, and absolute responsivity lives in the detector model'.
LUT spacing: §3.2(b) line 164 '0.05-0.1 K spacing' vs scripts/generate_luts.py line 9 and ir-radiometry skill line 64 '0.05 K' (fixed). 200-1000 K at 0.05 K is 16001 entries, quoted as '~16k'.

Material schema wrapper and fields: §12.3 lines 907-908 nest under a `materials:` key; .claude/skills/thermal-materials/SKILL.md lines 136-150 show the material at top level and add a `source` field the spec lacks. CLAUDE.md layout assigns 'pydantic schemas for … material' to config/ but 'library + loader' to materials/ — the split is undefined in the spec.

Material emissivity representation: §12.3 line 916 requires a spectral CSV (0.3-15 um) while §16.2 lines 1262-1278 supply only scalar per-band eps values and Appendix A #3 line 1388 states emissivity is grey within a band — no scalar fallback is defined in the schema.

T_ref/T_span vs LUT range: §13.3 line 981 (T_ref = 200 K, T_span = 800 K) and §3.2(b) line 164 (LUT on [200, 1000] K) define the same domain independently; neither the spec nor constants.py defines it once.
Reference camera HFOV: §16.1 line 1253 '14 mm, 32 deg HFOV' vs 2 atan(640 x 0.012 mm / (2 x 14 mm)) = 30.7 deg from the §12.2/§16.1 pitch and resolution — 4% apart.

Tooling vs declared support: tests/unit/test_planck.py lines 37, 64-65, 80 use `np.trapezoid` (NumPy >= 2.0) while pyproject.toml line 11 allows `numpy>=1.24`; pyproject.toml has no `types-PyYAML` and no `yaml.*` mypy override although `pyyaml` is a runtime dependency and mypy is strict on src/irsim.

Makefile `luts` target (`--configs configs/sensors --out data/lut`) provides no data-root argument, while the generate_luts.py docstring expects to load R(lambda) from data/spectra/ — the script's path convention is unspecified.

Layering test scope: tests/unit/test_layering.py line 12 forbids {omni, pxr, isaacsim, warp, carb}; CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #1 lists omni, pxr, isaacsim, warp only (test is stricter; harmless, but `irsim_isaac` itself is not forbidden by either).

Sky model parameters (§5.3 lines 310-314: DeltaT_clear, q, cloud) and atmosphere table indices (§7.2 line 471: band, atmosphere, humidity, visibility) have no schema anywhere in §12 although configs/atmospheres/ exists and CLAUDE.md assigns its schema to config/.
